nodes.label: Mechanisms identified in the spectra work (Register 720)
nodes.rationale: Staged for the mathematics register in mathreg.py's format (key, statement, grade, source, dependencies) but held back: the register has held mathematical objects and these are physical mechanisms, so whether they enter as a new family P.* or as an appendix waits on the Spectra Compendium closing. Evidence and falsifiers are recorded now, while fresh, rather than reconstructed later.

nodes.label: P.qdt — the quantum defect measures core penetration
nodes.rationale: The root mechanism from which the rest follow; the compendium tests it four independent ways without ever encoding it. Falsified by any species whose defect fails to fall monotonically with l. Registers 693, 707, 713, 714.

nodes.label: P.lcollapse — the l-collapse
nodes.rationale: The defect falls monotonically with l and reaches zero by f, because the centrifugal barrier pushes the orbital outward until it no longer reaches the core. 103 adjacent-l pairs, zero inverted; falsified by one clean inversion at a measurable defect.

nodes.label: P.iso — the isoelectronic ladder
nodes.rationale: For fixed element and l the defect falls as core charge rises, because a tighter potential holds the outer electron further out. Where the defect exceeds 0.3, 15 of 15 fall; below 0.3 only 10 of 20, which is chance — so the threshold is part of the claim.

nodes.label: P.dcollapse — the d-collapse competes with the ladder
nodes.rationale: As charge rises the d orbital contracts and penetrates more, the opposite of P.iso; where the defect is large P.iso dominates and where small P.dcollapse can win. All ten apparent P.iso exceptions are d, all small, all in this direction — so the exception set is explained rather than excused. Falsified by an s or p exception, which this cannot explain.

nodes.label: P.coreblind — the defect does not depend on the parent term
nodes.rationale: A defect belongs to l and the core's charge, not to which state the core is in: Ne II's two parent cores 26,000 cm-1 apart give the same defect at ns and nd.

nodes.label: P.jj — J-inconsistency marks where LS coupling fails
nodes.rationale: A defect should not depend on J; where it does, the coupling scheme has changed. 32 of 38 series consistent within 0.05, and the six failures are heavy or strongly split systems where jj has displaced LS. Falsified by J-inconsistency in a light, weakly split system.

nodes.label: P.perturb — a large spread is a perturbed series, not bad data
nodes.rationale: Where a state of the same symmetry cuts through a Rydberg run the defect scatters, and the scatter is a measurement of the perturbation rather than noise: Al I nd spread 0.6297 against Zn I np 0.0033 unperturbed.

nodes.label: P.converge — a Rydberg series measures its own limit
nodes.rationale: Ba III's limit fitted at 289,118 against a published 289,100 +/- 20 — eighteen apart, inside the error bar — with the fine structure closing three ways at 17,550 / 17,566 / 17,549.5.

nodes.label: P.trunc — truncation removes channels and degrades those it leaves
nodes.rationale: Cutting a series at low n takes most channels rather than a proportional share and widens the defect of the survivors: Ne I 33 Handbook levels give 0 channels where the full ASD table gives 4, and Ba III three-member runs spread 0.07-0.10 against 0.014-0.027 on the same series at ten and fifteen members.

nodes.label: P.buildlimit — a limit can be constructed from two spectra and tested by convergence
nodes.rationale: Where a series converges on a state above its own ionisation threshold no published limit exists, so the limit is a sum of two numbers from two spectra and the convergence is the test that the sum is right: Ne I at 173,929.75 + 217,047.598 gives delta = +0.8408, spread 0.0191 over ten members, landing where P.lcollapse requires.
